name: Titan (Redis on TiKV)
tagline: Redis-protocol NoSQL layer on TiKV from Meitu; dormant since 2021.
description: Titan is a stateless Go service that speaks the Redis protocol and stores data in a TiKV cluster, giving Redis-style strings, hashes, lists, sets and sorted sets distributed transactions, multi-tenancy and horizontal scale beyond one machine's RAM. It was built and open-sourced by Meitu's infrastructure team in 2018 and later moved to the DistributedIO GitHub organisation. You run TiKV and PD yourself and point redis-cli or any Redis client at Titan. Development stopped in 2021 (last tag v0.6.0, January 2020), so today it is mainly a reference design; Apache Kvrocks and Pika cover the same 'disk-backed Redis' niche with active communities.
statusNote: No commits since October 2021 (last tag v0.6.0, Jan 2020); effectively abandoned. Apache Kvrocks or Pika are maintained alternatives.

scale.notes: Stateless Titan nodes scale out in front of TiKV, which shards and replicates data with Raft.

strengths: Redis wire compatibility, so existing Redis clients and redis-cli work unchanged
Data lives in TiKV, so capacity is not bounded by RAM and survives node loss via Raft replication
Distributed transactions with strong consistency across keys
Stateless proxy tier is easy to scale horizontally
weaknesses: Abandoned since 2021; no security fixes or new Redis command coverage
Requires operating a full TiKV + PD cluster underneath
Higher latency than in-memory Redis because every operation is a TiKV transaction
Incomplete Redis command set (no Lua scripting, limited cluster semantics)
useCases: Reference design for a Redis protocol layer over a distributed KV store
Legacy deployments already running it on TiKV
